# Story 04 — Implement Identity & Access Management (Backend) (Story: 4)

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 completed: backend skeleton with FastAPI app factory, `Settings`, async SQLAlchemy engine, `/health` endpoint, and the empty `app/modules/identity_access/` onion skeleton (`api/`, `application/`, `domain/`, `infrastructure/`). See `backend/README.md` and `backend/docs/architecture.md`.
- Local Postgres reachable via `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://crm:crm@localhost:5432/crm` (see `backend/README.md` ~lines 51–83).
- Confirm no prior identity plans have already introduced JWT/RBAC. This story establishes those foundations for the first time.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver the full Identity & Access backend module for the CRM in a single vertical slice, respecting the Onion layering enforced by `backend/tests/test_layering.py`:

1. Customer self-registration and admin-driven user creation persisted in PostgreSQL with hashed passwords.
2. JWT access-token + refresh-token authentication with configurable expiry, refresh-token rotation, and server-side revocation on logout.
3. Role-Based Access Control: users → roles → permissions, evaluated by a FastAPI dependency on every protected route.
4. Full CRUD APIs for users, roles, permissions, plus role assignment and role-permission mapping.
5. Consistent validation and error responses covering all AC-14 error classes.

**Out of scope:** frontend integration (already stubbed in `frontend/src/features/authentication/`), password reset / email verification flows, OAuth/social login, multi-tenant isolation, audit logging, Alembic *automation* beyond the initial revisions this story adds.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** Only `GET /health` exists; identity router is empty; no users, roles, permissions, tokens, or hashing exist.
- **New behaviour:** All identity endpoints listed under "API surface" below are mounted under `/identity`, every non-auth endpoint requires a valid JWT, and admin-scoped endpoints additionally require the corresponding permission.
- Passwords are stored **only** as bcrypt hashes; the API **never** returns password fields.
- Refresh tokens are stored server-side (hashed) and revocable; access tokens are stateless JWTs.
- JWT signing secret is loaded from env (`JWT_SECRET`); the app must fail fast at startup if it is missing (mirror the existing `DATABASE_URL` behaviour described in `backend/README.md` ~lines 80–83).

`jwt_secret` is **required** (no default) → pydantic raises `ValidationError` at startup exactly like `database_url`. Document the new vars in `backend/README.md`'s Configuration table (~lines 63–73) and add matching entries to `backend/.env.example`.

### 2 — Domain layer (`backend/app/modules/identity_access/domain/`)

**No imports of `sqlalchemy`, `fastapi`, or `pydantic`.** Pure Python + dataclasses / stdlib only. `backend/tests/test_layering.py` enforces this.

Create the following files (each a small dataclass or protocol; keep every class in its own module for testability):

- `entities/user.py` — `@dataclass class User: id: UUID; email: str; hashed_password: str; full_name: str; is_active: bool; is_customer: bool; created_at: datetime; updated_at: datetime; role_ids: set[UUID]`.
- `entities/role.py` — `@dataclass class Role: id: UUID; name: str; description: str | None; permission_ids: set[UUID]`.
- `entities/permission.py` — `@dataclass class Permission: id: UUID; code: str; description: str | None`. `code` uses dotted-notation (e.g. `User.View`, per intake §8).
- `entities/refresh_token.py` — `@dataclass class RefreshToken: id: UUID; user_id: UUID; token_hash: str; issued_at: datetime; expires_at: datetime; revoked_at: datetime | None`.
- `value_objects/email.py` — `Email` value object validating format via a compiled regex (no `pydantic`, no `email-validator` in domain).
- `value_objects/password.py` — `RawPassword` VO enforcing length ≥ 8, must contain letter + digit; raises `WeakPasswordError`.
- `errors.py` — module-scoped exceptions: `IdentityError`, `InvalidCredentialsError`, `DuplicateAccountError`, `UserNotFoundError`, `RoleNotFoundError`, `PermissionNotFoundError`, `RefreshTokenInvalidError`, `RefreshTokenExpiredError`, `RefreshTokenRevokedError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `WeakPasswordError`, `InvalidEmailError`.
- `services/authorization.py` — pure function `def has_permission(user_permission_codes: set[str], required: str) -> bool`.
- `ports/repositories.py` — `typing.Protocol` interfaces: `UserRepository`, `RoleRepository`, `PermissionRepository`, `RefreshTokenRepository`. Method signatures use domain entities only. Include `find_by_email`, `find_by_id`, `add`, `update`, `delete`, `list_all(limit, offset)`, `find_by_ids`, plus refresh-token-specific `find_by_hash`, `revoke`, `revoke_all_for_user`.
- `ports/hashing.py` — `class PasswordHasher(Protocol): def hash(self, raw: str) -> str; def verify(self, raw: str, hashed: str) -> bool`.
- `ports/tokens.py` — `AccessTokenIssuer` (encode/decode) and `RefreshTokenIssuer` (generate opaque token + hash) protocols.
- `ports/clock.py` — `class Clock(Protocol): def now(self) -> datetime`. Allows freezegun-free tests to inject deterministic time.

### 3 — Application layer (`backend/app/modules/identity_access/application/`)

**Allowed imports:** `domain` + stdlib + `typing`. No `sqlalchemy`, no `fastapi`, no `pydantic`.

Create use-case classes; each class receives its ports via `__init__` for testability:

- `use_cases/register_customer.py` — `RegisterCustomer(user_repo, hasher, clock)`. Validates email + password VOs, checks duplicates, persists with `is_customer=True`, `is_active=True`, no roles assigned.
- `use_cases/login.py` — `Login(user_repo, refresh_repo, hasher, access_issuer, refresh_issuer, clock, settings_ttl)`. Returns a DTO `LoginResult(access_token, refresh_token, access_expires_in, refresh_expires_in, user_summary)`. Emits `InvalidCredentialsError` for unknown email **or** wrong password (identical message — AC-12).
- `use_cases/refresh_token.py` — `RefreshToken(refresh_repo, user_repo, access_issuer, refresh_issuer, clock)`. Implements **rotation**: on success, mark the presented token revoked and issue a new pair.
- `use_cases/logout.py` — `Logout(refresh_repo, clock)`. Revokes the presented refresh token (idempotent — a second call is a no-op).
- `use_cases/users/` — `CreateUser`, `ListUsers`, `GetUser`, `UpdateUser`, `SetUserActive`, `DeleteUser`, `AssignRolesToUser`, `GetUserRoles`.
- `use_cases/roles/` — `CreateRole`, `ListRoles`, `GetRole`, `UpdateRole`, `DeleteRole`, `AssignPermissionsToRole`, `RemovePermissionsFromRole`, `GetRolePermissions`.
- `use_cases/permissions/` — `CreatePermission`, `ListPermissions`, `GetPermission`, `UpdatePermission`, `DeletePermission`.
- `dto.py` — small `@dataclass(frozen=True)` DTOs used for use-case inputs/outputs (`UserSummary`, `RoleSummary`, `PermissionSummary`, `LoginResult`, `TokenPair`). **No pydantic here** — pydantic lives at the API edge.
- `authorization.py` — helper `resolve_effective_permissions(user, role_repo, permission_repo) -> set[str]` used by the authorization dependency.

### 4 — Infrastructure layer (`backend/app/modules/identity_access/infrastructure/`)

**Allowed imports:** everything (`sqlalchemy`, `passlib`, `pyjwt`, `secrets`, etc.). Implements the domain ports.

#### 4.1 ORM models

`orm/models.py` — SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models inheriting `app.shared.infrastructure.orm.base.Base`. UUID primary keys via `sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.UUID(as_uuid=True)`.

- `users` — `id`, `email` (unique, citext-like via `String(320)` + `Index` `UniqueConstraint` on `func.lower(email)`), `hashed_password`, `full_name`, `is_active`, `is_customer`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
- `roles` — `id`, `name` (unique), `description`.
- `permissions` — `id`, `code` (unique), `description`.
- `user_roles` — composite PK (`user_id`, `role_id`) with FKs and `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- `role_permissions` — composite PK (`role_id`, `permission_id`) with FKs and `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- `refresh_tokens` — `id`, `user_id` (FK, index), `token_hash` (unique, `String(128)`), `issued_at`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at` (nullable), `Index("ix_refresh_tokens_user_active", "user_id", "revoked_at")`.

#### 4.2 Repositories

`repositories/sqlalchemy_user_repository.py`, `..._role_repository.py`, `..._permission_repository.py`, `..._refresh_token_repository.py` — each takes an `AsyncSession` in `__init__` and implements the matching domain `Protocol`. Include mappers `_to_entity` / `_to_model` between ORM and domain dataclasses; never leak ORM types outside the module.

#### 4.3 Security services

- `security/password_hasher.py` — `PasslibBcryptHasher(rounds: int)` implementing `PasswordHasher` port using `passlib.context.CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], bcrypt__rounds=rounds)`.
- `security/jwt_access_token.py` — `PyJWTAccessTokenIssuer(secret, algorithm, ttl_seconds, clock)`. Claims: `sub` (user id), `email`, `roles` (list of role names), `permissions` (list of codes), `iat`, `exp`, `type="access"`. `decode()` raises `TokenExpiredError` / `TokenInvalidError` mapped from `jwt.ExpiredSignatureError` / `jwt.InvalidTokenError`.
- `security/refresh_token_service.py` — `SecretsRefreshTokenIssuer(ttl_seconds, clock)`: uses `secrets.token_urlsafe(64)` for the opaque token and `hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest()` for the stored `token_hash`. The plaintext token is returned to the client **only once**; only the hash is persisted.
- `security/system_clock.py` — `SystemClock` returning `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.

#### 4.4 Composition helpers

`composition.py` — factory functions used by API dependencies: `build_password_hasher(settings)`, `build_access_issuer(settings, clock)`, `build_refresh_issuer(settings, clock)`, `build_user_repo(session)`, etc. Keeps `api/` slim and avoids repeated wiring code.

#### 4.5 Alembic setup & initial migration

- Create `backend/alembic.ini` and `backend/alembic/` (`env.py`, `versions/`). `env.py` imports every module's ORM models (initially only identity_access) to populate `Base.metadata` and reads `DATABASE_URL` from `Settings`.
- First revision `versions/0001_identity_access.py` creates all six tables above with the indexes/constraints listed in 4.1.
- Document `alembic upgrade head` in `backend/README.md` under a new "Migrations" section replacing the "Migrations for domain tables (no Alembic yet)" bullet at ~line 121.

### 5 — API layer (`backend/app/modules/identity_access/api/`)

**Allowed imports:** `fastapi`, `pydantic`, `application`, `infrastructure` (composition only), `domain` (for exception types only).

#### 5.1 Router composition

Replace `backend/app/modules/identity_access/api/router.py` body:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

from .routers import auth as auth_router
from .routers import users as users_router
from .routers import roles as roles_router
from .routers import permissions as permissions_router

router = APIRouter()
router.include_router(auth_router.router, prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])
router.include_router(users_router.router, prefix="/users", tags=["users"])
router.include_router(roles_router.router, prefix="/roles", tags=["roles"])
router.include_router(permissions_router.router, prefix="/permissions", tags=["permissions"])
```

The top-level mount in `backend/app/main.py` line 29 stays (`prefix="/identity"`), giving final paths like `POST /identity/auth/login`.

#### 5.2 Schemas (`api/schemas/`)

Pydantic v2 models for every request/response. Response models must not include `hashed_password`. Examples:

```python
class RegisterCustomerRequest(BaseModel):
    email: EmailStr
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    full_name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)

class LoginRequest(BaseModel):
    email: EmailStr
    password: str

class TokenPairResponse(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    refresh_token: str
    token_type: Literal["Bearer"] = "Bearer"
    access_expires_in: int
    refresh_expires_in: int

class UserResponse(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str
    is_active: bool
    is_customer: bool
    roles: list[RoleSummaryResponse]
```

#### 5.3 Endpoints

Auth (`routers/auth.py`):
- `POST /identity/auth/register` — public. Body `RegisterCustomerRequest` → 201 `UserResponse`.
- `POST /identity/auth/login` — public. Body `LoginRequest` → 200 `TokenPairResponse`.
- `POST /identity/auth/refresh` — public. Body `RefreshRequest{ refresh_token }` → 200 `TokenPairResponse` (new pair, old token revoked).
- `POST /identity/auth/logout` — requires access token. Body `RefreshRequest` → 204.
- `GET /identity/auth/me` — requires access token → 200 `UserResponse`.

Users (`routers/users.py`) — all require permission `User.<Action>`:
- `GET /identity/users` (`User.View`), `POST /identity/users` (`User.Create`), `GET /identity/users/{id}` (`User.View`), `PATCH /identity/users/{id}` (`User.Update`), `PATCH /identity/users/{id}/active` (`User.Update`, body `{is_active: bool}`), `DELETE /identity/users/{id}` (`User.Delete`), `PUT /identity/users/{id}/roles` (`User.AssignRole`, body `{role_ids: list[UUID]}`), `GET /identity/users/{id}/roles` (`User.View`).

Roles (`routers/roles.py`) — permissions `Role.View/Create/Update/Delete/AssignPermission`:
- `GET/POST /identity/roles`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /identity/roles/{id}`, `PUT /identity/roles/{id}/permissions`, `GET /identity/roles/{id}/permissions`.

Permissions (`routers/permissions.py`) — permissions `Permission.View/Create/Update/Delete`:
- `GET/POST /identity/permissions`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /identity/permissions/{id}`.

#### 5.4 Dependencies (`api/dependencies.py`)

- `get_db_session()` — thin wrapper around `app.shared.infrastructure.database.get_session` for FastAPI `Depends`.
- `get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme), session = Depends(get_db_session))` — decodes JWT via `PyJWTAccessTokenIssuer`, loads user from repo, raises `HTTPException(401)` on invalid/expired/missing tokens. Uses `HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)` so the missing-token case can raise 401 with a body matching AC-14 rather than FastAPI's default 403.
- `require_permission(code: str)` — factory returning a dependency that resolves effective permissions via `resolve_effective_permissions` and raises `HTTPException(403, detail="insufficient_permissions")` when the code is absent.

#### 5.5 Error handlers (`api/error_handlers.py`, registered in `app/main.py`)

Map each domain exception to a consistent JSON envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "invalid_credentials", "message": "Invalid email or password." } }
```

Mapping:

| Exception | HTTP | `error.code` |
|---|---|---|
| `InvalidCredentialsError` | 401 | `invalid_credentials` |
| `RefreshTokenInvalidError` | 401 | `invalid_refresh_token` |
| `RefreshTokenExpiredError` | 401 | `expired_refresh_token` |
| `RefreshTokenRevokedError` | 401 | `revoked_refresh_token` |
| Missing/invalid access token | 401 | `unauthenticated` |
| Expired access token | 401 | `token_expired` |
| `PermissionDeniedError` | 403 | `insufficient_permissions` |
| `DuplicateAccountError` | 409 | `duplicate_account` |
| `UserNotFoundError` / `RoleNotFoundError` / `PermissionNotFoundError` | 404 | `not_found` |
| `WeakPasswordError` / `InvalidEmailError` | 422 | `validation_failed` |
| pydantic `RequestValidationError` | 422 | `validation_failed` (override the default handler to reuse the envelope) |
| Uncaught `Exception` | 500 | `internal_error` |

Register handlers in `create_app()` in `backend/app/main.py` immediately after `app = FastAPI(...)` on line 27.

### 6 — Bootstrap / seed

`backend/app/modules/identity_access/infrastructure/seed.py` — idempotent function `async def seed_default_permissions_and_admin(session, hasher, settings)` that inserts the base permission codes listed in "AC-08 / examples" (`User.View`, `User.Create`, `User.Update`, `User.Delete`, `Role.View`, `Role.Create`, `Role.Update`, `Role.Delete`, `Role.AssignPermission`, `Permission.View`, `Permission.Create`, `Permission.Update`, `Permission.Delete`, `User.AssignRole`) and an `admin` role with all of them. If env var `IDENTITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `IDENTITY_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` are set, create an initial admin user with that role. Call it once from `lifespan()` in `backend/app/main.py` (~lines 14–20) **after** `init_engine`, wrapped in a try/except that logs and swallows `SQLAlchemyError` so the app still boots when the DB is offline (mirroring the health-check philosophy in `backend/docs/architecture.md` ~lines 46–48).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing `JWT_SECRET` at startup** → pydantic `ValidationError` before the app serves traffic, matching the `DATABASE_URL` behaviour described in `backend/README.md` ~lines 80–83. Enforced in `Settings` (Task 1).
- **Case-insensitive email duplicates** (`Foo@x.com` vs `foo@x.com`) → normalise to lowercase in `Email` VO **and** enforce the `UniqueConstraint` on `func.lower(email)` (Task 4.1). `RegisterCustomer` catches `IntegrityError` from the repo and re-raises `DuplicateAccountError`.
- **Timing attack on login** → always call `hasher.verify` even when the user does not exist (use a dummy hash constant) before raising `InvalidCredentialsError` (Task 3 `Login`).
- **Refresh-token replay after rotation** → old token's `revoked_at` is set inside the same transaction as the new token's insert; a second use of the old token hits `RefreshTokenRevokedError`. Enforced in `RefreshToken` use case (Task 3) + `RefreshTokenRepository.revoke` (Task 4.2).
- **Clock skew** → tests inject a `FrozenClock` (Task 3 ports/clock.py). Production uses `SystemClock`; TTLs are exact seconds so ±1s skew is acceptable.
- **Deleting a role that is still assigned to users** → cascade via `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `user_roles` (Task 4.1) so no orphan rows remain. `DeleteRole` returns 204 even when no users held the role.
- **Deleting the last permission from an admin role** — allowed; there is no "protected role" concept in this story. Document as a known operational risk in code comments on `DeleteRole` / `RemovePermissionsFromRole`.
- **JWT tampering / wrong algorithm** — `pyjwt.decode(..., algorithms=[settings.jwt_algorithm])` rejects `alg=none` and mismatched algorithms. `get_current_user` returns 401 `unauthenticated`.
- **Concurrent logins for same user** — each login inserts a new refresh-token row; logout revokes only the presented one. `revoke_all_for_user` is available for future "logout everywhere" but not exposed by an endpoint in this story.
- **Password containing unicode / >72 bytes** — bcrypt truncates at 72 bytes; document in `RawPassword` VO and enforce `len(raw.encode("utf-8")) <= 72` to fail fast with `WeakPasswordError`.
- **Partial migration state** — Alembic revision `0001` is atomic in Postgres transactional DDL; on failure re-run `alembic downgrade base` then `alembic upgrade head`. Covered in Migration / Rollback.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** `alembic upgrade head` runs revision `0001_identity_access` creating all six tables and their indexes.
- **Rollback:** `alembic downgrade base` drops the tables (all cascades already declared).
- **Half-applied state risk:** Postgres runs DDL in a transaction, so the migration either commits fully or rolls back. If a manual `psql` change diverged, run `alembic stamp base` then re-apply.
- **Secret rotation:** rotating `JWT_SECRET` invalidates all outstanding access tokens (desired) but does **not** invalidate refresh tokens because they are opaque; run a `DELETE FROM refresh_tokens` (or a bespoke script) if you need to force re-login.

3. **Migrations apply cleanly:** in `backend/`, `alembic upgrade head` against a fresh local Postgres (see `backend/README.md` ~lines 55–57). Confirm `\dt` in `psql` lists `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `user_roles`, `role_permissions`, `refresh_tokens`.
4. **Backend tests:** in `backend/`, run `pytest -q`. All new and existing tests pass.
5. **Layering guard:** `pytest backend/tests/test_layering.py -q` — must remain green.
6. **Runtime smoke:** in `backend/`, `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`, then:
   - `curl -X POST localhost:8000/identity/auth/register -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"a@b.co","password":"Passw0rd!","full_name":"A B"}'` → 201.
   - `curl -X POST localhost:8000/identity/auth/login ...` → 200 with `access_token` + `refresh_token`.
   - `curl localhost:8000/identity/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer <access>"` → 200.
   - `curl localhost:8000/identity/users -H "Authorization: Bearer <customer-access>"` → 403 `insufficient_permissions`.
7. **Regression:** `curl localhost:8000/health` still returns `{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}`.
8. **Frontend regression:** no change expected. Optionally in `frontend/`, run `pnpm test` to confirm existing tests still pass.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] AC-01 — `POST /identity/auth/register` creates a customer, validates required/format/duplicate/password rules, stores only bcrypt hashes.
- [ ] AC-02 — `POST /identity/auth/login` returns access + refresh tokens with configurable TTLs; no password ever appears in a response.
- [ ] AC-03 — Access token is a valid JWT with `sub`, `email`, `roles`, `permissions`, `exp`; invalid/expired tokens are rejected by `get_current_user`.
- [ ] AC-04 — `POST /identity/auth/refresh` issues a new pair only for valid, unexpired, un-revoked refresh tokens; presented token is rotated.
- [ ] AC-05 — `POST /identity/auth/logout` revokes the refresh token; subsequent refresh with it returns 401.
- [ ] AC-06 — Full user CRUD + activate/deactivate + role assignment endpoints exist, each gated on the matching `User.*` permission.
- [ ] AC-07 — Full role CRUD endpoints exist; duplicate role names rejected with 409.
- [ ] AC-08 — Permission listing/CRUD and role-permission mapping endpoints exist; authorization dependency reads live role-permission relationships.
- [ ] AC-09 — `PUT /identity/users/{id}/roles` assigns/replaces roles; effective permissions returned by `/auth/me` reflect current assignments.
- [ ] AC-10 — All non-auth endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer` and the `require_permission(...)` dependency.
- [ ] AC-11 — Validation errors surface via the shared error envelope (`error.code == "validation_failed"`).
- [ ] AC-12 — `JWT_SECRET` loaded from env; passwords hashed with bcrypt (`passlib`); never returned by any response schema.
- [ ] AC-13 — Alembic revision `0001_identity_access` creates all six tables with the constraints listed; CRUD verified end-to-end.
- [ ] AC-14 — Every error class in the table under Task 5.5 has a mapped handler and a covering test.

- [ ] AC-16 — Every CRUD + auth endpoint has success + failure test coverage per the Test Plan section.
